page: Microsoft Azure D2ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with 2 threads, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 118 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include a GPU.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Due to its high 4.5 GHz clock speed, the server delivers top-tier single-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scores, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, because it is limited to a single physical core, its multi-core capabilities are weak, placing in the bottom 25% for multi-core Geekbench, stress-ng multi-core, and software compilation. Memory performance is average for large block reads and writes, but weak for small block cached reads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ads_v7 offers a highly dense single-thread compute profile relative to its resource class, making it an economical option for workloads that do not scale across multiple cores. It is poorly suited for multi-threaded tasks, database operations, or high-throughput web serving, which all score in the bottom 25%. Instead, this instance is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded text processing, basic scripting, and entry-level development environments that benefit from high single-core clock speeds without requiring massive parallel processing.
